title: Token Optimization Strategies for LLM-Based Oracle-to-PostgreSQL Migration
problem: LLM-based Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration is constrained by high token consumption, long-context degradation, dialect-specific semantic differences, and semantic drift during query transformation.
key_idea: Token optimization is formalized as a constrained transformation problem, and twelve strategies are systematically evaluated to balance cost, syntactic validity, semantic preservation, and structural fidelity.
method: Twelve token optimization strategies (e.g., baseline representation, context pruning, minification, DSL-based semantic compression, adaptive routing, AST-based minification) are formalized and evaluated on Oracle SQL queries.
dataset_or_scenario: Samples of 10 and 100 Oracle SQL queries.
metrics: Valid Syntax Rate, Exact Match, Semantic Match, CodeBLEU, Token Efficiency.
results_summary: Mild context pruning achieves 89.75% Semantic Match (vs. 89.80% baseline); adaptive routing reduces input tokens by 8.72% and output tokens by 5.49% while maintaining 88.40% Semantic Match and increasing Token Efficiency by 6.67%; aggressive schema distillation increases Token Efficiency by 132.22% but reduces Semantic Match by 44.50 percentage points.
limitations: The study is limited to Oracle-to-PostgreSQL migration and may not generalize to other database migration tasks; aggressive optimization strategies can significantly degrade semantic match.

title: Do LLMs Favor Their Providers? Measuring Vertical Integration Bias in Code Generation
problem: Large Language Models (LLMs) affiliated with specific providers may exhibit bias towards their own ecosystem in code generation, potentially constraining developer choices and increasing provider dependence.
key_idea: Introduces the concept of Vertical Integration Bias (VIB) and a benchmark (VIBench) to measure this bias in direct and agentic code generation across provider-selectable scenarios.
method: Evaluates 10 frontier provider-affiliated models against 3 non-affiliated controls using VIBench, a benchmark with 20 provider-selectable software-integration scenarios, measuring bias in both direct and agentic code generation.
dataset_or_scenario: VIBench benchmark with 20 provider-selectable software-integration scenarios.
metrics: Percentage points (pp) difference in favor of provider's ecosystem.
results_summary: Six of ten affiliated models show statistically significant VIB in direct generation (up to +18.8 pp), and agentic workflows amplify VIB to +39.2 pp, with early ecosystem choices persisting in downstream files up to 90.3%.

title: Efficient and Scalable Provenance Tracking for LLM-Generated Code Snippets
problem: Classical fingerprint-based plagiarism detectors are impractical for billion-scale corpora used to train modern code LLMs due to linear-time search, and there is a need for scalable provenance tracking to address legal and ethical concerns.
key_idea: A hybrid two-stage pipeline that first narrows candidate snippets via vector search and then re-ranks using Winnowing on exact fingerprints, achieving logarithmic-time query complexity.
method: Introduces SOURCETRACKER, a 300M-parameter encoder for code retrieval, and HYBRIDSOURCETRACKER (HST) pipeline: vector search for candidate selection followed by Winnowing-based re-ranking.
dataset_or_scenario: 10M-snippet subset of THESTACKV2 dataset with verbatim and adapted snippets (identifier renaming); in vitro 100k-snippet search space.
metrics: Mean reciprocal rank (MRR); comparison with Winnowing for 30-token and >=60-token fragments.
results_summary: Hybrid approach achieves MRR on par with Winnowing for 30-token fragments and outperforms by up to 5.4% for windows >=60 tokens, with logarithmic-time complexity.
limitations: Evaluation limited to a 10M-snippet subset; real-world scalability to billion-scale corpora not fully demonstrated.

title: Functional Entropy: Predicting Functional Correctness in LLM-Generated Code with Uncertainty Quantification
problem: Large language models often generate functionally incorrect code, and uncertainty quantification methods for detecting hallucinations in natural language have not been systematically evaluated for code generation.
key_idea: Introduces functional equivalence methods, including functional entropy, which replace natural language inference-based semantic equivalence with an LLM-based functional equivalence assessment to better predict functional correctness.
method: Systematically evaluates uncertainty quantification techniques for code generation across multiple languages, models, and problems; proposes functional equivalence methods that use LLM-based functional equivalence instead of NLI-based semantic equivalence.
dataset_or_scenario: Over 1,700 problems across three programming languages and five LLMs.
results_summary: Functional equivalence methods achieve top AUROC in 11 out of 15 model-benchmark combinations and the best calibration across most settings, outperforming NLI-based counterparts and other methods.

title: Rethinking Software Empirical Studies with Structural Causal Models
problem: Traditional statistical association methods in empirical software engineering (ESE) are limited in mitigating confounding bias, leading to potential false positives when evaluating causal relationships.
key_idea: Introduces CausalSE, a framework that operationalizes Judea Pearl's causal inference paradigm using Structural Causal Models (SCMs) to rigorously identify and quantify causal relationships in software experiments.
method: CausalSE applies SCMs and propensity score matching to control for confounding; demonstrated via a case study on prompt engineering strategies for code generation with GPT-3 using the Galeras dataset.
dataset_or_scenario: Galeras dataset; case study on prompt engineering strategies for code generation with GPT-3.
metrics: Not specified in the abstract (likely treatment effect estimates, p-values, or confidence intervals).
results_summary: Associational analyses suggested improvements from more complex prompts, but causal analysis found no significant treatment effect, highlighting false positive risks when confounding is unaddressed.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may depend on the specific case study and assumptions of SCMs.

title: Efficient Post-training of LLMs for Code Generation With Offline Reinforcement Learning
problem: Online reinforcement learning for code generation is resource-intensive due to LLM inference and verification, and the paper explores whether offline RL can be an effective alternative.
key_idea: Offline RL can be effectively applied to code-generating models by leveraging existing code datasets, offering a more efficient post-training strategy.
method: The paper applies offline reinforcement learning to code-generating models using existing code datasets, without requiring online inference or verification.
dataset_or_scenario: Existing code datasets (not specified in detail).
results_summary: Offline RL is shown to be an effective training strategy for improving LLM performance, especially beneficial for small LLMs and challenging coding problems.
limitations: The abstract does not specify limitations, but offline RL may rely on the quality and coverage of existing datasets.

title: From paper to benchmark: agentic, framework-based reproduction of under-specified methods in machine health intelligence
problem: Reproducing under-specified methods in Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) is difficult due to restricted data access, incomplete reporting, and implicit design choices that affect performance, and existing paper-to-code systems produce non-comparable implementations.
key_idea: Introducing agentic, framework-based PHM paper reproduction using a slot-binding interface that maps paper components into a shared benchmark framework, explicitly recording unresolved assumptions for consistent and comparable benchmarking.
method: An agent translates a paper into a shared PHM benchmark framework via a slot-binding interface that maps equations and protocol descriptions into structured components (task definitions, dataset adapters, windowing, targets, models, evaluators), and validates implementations against standardized task contracts and evaluation hooks.
metrics: Reproduction success, model-based code evaluation, framework binding of paper assumptions, cross-paper benchmark comparability under standardized protocols.
results_summary: Coupling agentic generation with a shared framework transforms paper reproduction into executable, assumption-aware, and systematically comparable benchmark implementations.

title: GUI Agents for Continual Game Generation
problem: Existing game generation approaches treat it as one-shot translation from prompt to artifact, failing to detect interaction-level failures and lacking evaluation of playability.
key_idea: Using GUI agents as both objective evaluators and subjective playtesters in a continual loop to generate and improve playable games.
method: Introduces PlaytestArena for evaluation with 200 browser-based game tasks and rubrics adjudicated by a GUI agent, and Play2Code where a game agent and GUI agent operate in a sustained loop with shared memory for iterative game generation.
dataset_or_scenario: 200 browser-based game generation tasks across eight genres with rubrics of expected in-play behaviors.
results_summary: Play2Code achieves a 66.8% rubric pass-rate, improving over single-pass and agentic-coding baselines by 37.1 and 14.6 points respectively.

title: When Confidence Misleads: Suffix Anchoring and Anchor-Proximity Confidence Modulation for Diffusion Language Models
problem: Confidence-based position selection in fully non-autoregressive diffusion language models can be misleading, causing incomplete generation due to high-confidence EOT tokens and premature decoding of anchor-adjacent tokens due to local overconfidence near suffix anchors.
key_idea: Inserting a short suffix anchor encourages response completion, and modulating confidence near the anchor according to decoding progress prevents premature decoding of adjacent tokens.
method: Suffix-Anchored Confidence Modulation: a training-free method that inserts a short suffix anchor and adjusts confidence scores near the anchor based on decoding progress.
dataset_or_scenario: Text-only reasoning, vision-language reasoning, and code-generation benchmarks.
results_summary: The method consistently improves confidence-based fully non-autoregressive decoding, outperforms explicit EOT suppression, and preserves the parallel decoding advantage.

title: Beyond pass@k: Redundancy-Aware RLVR for Multi-Sample Code Generation
problem: Current verifier-based reinforcement learning (RLVR) methods for code generation improve executable correctness but may increase redundancy among sampled programs, reducing diversity and harming performance under finite sampling budgets.
key_idea: Introduces redundancy-aware RLVR by incorporating direct anti-redundancy rewards based on JPlag similarity to discourage near-duplicate generations, improving finite-budget executable performance.
method: Augments RLVR with anti-redundancy rewards computed from JPlag similarity between sampled programs, and compares against correctness-only RLVR and Pass@k-aware objectives across models and benchmarks.
dataset_or_scenario: Evaluated across 3 models and 3 benchmarks (not specified in abstract).
metrics: Executable correctness under finite sampling budgets, redundancy measured via JPlag similarity.
results_summary: Redundancy-aware RLVR reliably improves finite-budget executable performance, often matching or outperforming specialized Pass@k-aware objectives, while reducing redundancy compared to correctness-only RLVR.
limitations: Not specified in the abstract; may depend on JPlag similarity thresholds and generalizability to other code domains.
